title.justification: The title 'Reward is enough' reflects the central hypothesis of the paper, which proposes that the maximisation of reward is a sufficient driving force behind the various expressions and abilities associated with intelligence.
title.quote: In this article we hypothesise that intelligence, and its associated abilities, can be understood as subserving the maximisation of reward.

analysis.description: The paper hypothesizes that intelligence and its associated abilities can be driven solely by the maximisation of reward, negating the need for specialized problem formulations for each ability. It argues that reinforcement learning agents maximising rewards can exhibit forms of intelligence comparable to natural intelligence, thus proposing a pathway towards achieving artificial general intelligence.

type.justification: The paper puts forward a hypothesis and explores its implications for understanding intelligence, rather than conducting empirical experiments.
type.quote: In this article we hypothesise that intelligence, and its associated abilities, can be understood as subserving the maximisation of reward.

name.justification: The paper centralizes on the concept of reinforcement learning as the main approach to achieve artificial general intelligence through the maximization of reward.
name.quote: Accordingly, reward is enough to drive behaviour that exhibits abilities studied in natural and artificial intelligence... agents that learn through trial and error experience to maximise reward... could constitute a solution to artificial general intelligence.

name.justification: The paper broadly addresses the field of artificial intelligence through the lens of reward maximisation as a pathway to general intelligence.
name.quote: This is in contrast to the view that specialised problem formulations are needed for each ability, based on other signals or objectives.

name.justification: The paper explores the concept of artificial general intelligence as the ultimate goal of maximizing reward-based learning systems.
name.quote: Therefore that powerful reinforcement learning agents could constitute a solution to artificial general intelligence.

name.justification: The paper references AlphaZero as a model that exemplifies the principle that maximising a reward signal (winning a game) leads to intelligent behaviour.
name.quote: AlphaZero focused instead on a singular goal: maximising a reward signal that is 0 until the final step, and then + 1 for winning or − 1 for losing.

is_contributed.justification: The paper refers to AlphaZero as an existing model to support its hypothesis rather than contributing new model development.
is_contributed.quote: A recent salutary example of both problem and solution based on reward maximisation comes from the game of Go... AlphaZero focused instead on a singular goal.

is_executed.justification: The paper discusses AlphaZero in theoretical terms as an example of reward maximisation leading to intelligent behaviour.
is_executed.quote: This ultimately resulted in a deeper understanding of each ability – for example, discovering new opening sequences.

is_compared.justification: AlphaZero's performance and abilities are discussed in comparison with other existing models, illustrating the impact of its reward-maximising approach.
is_compared.quote: This ultimately resulted in a deeper understanding of each ability – for example, discovering new opening sequences.

referenced_paper_title.value: Mastering the game of go without human knowledge
referenced_paper_title.justification: The referenced paper on AlphaZero is included in the literature as a key example of reinforcement learning achieving sophisticated gameplay through reward maximisation.
referenced_paper_title.quote: AlphaZero [49] focused instead on a singular goal: maximising a reward signal.
